inputs.original_text: Thousands of people trying to use the immigration court system to secure legal status were instead arrested and detained. Court documents reportedly show prosecutors acknowledged that the May memo did not authorize those arrests, even though ICE lawyers allegedly invoked it to justify them. This is more than a legal technicality: it shows how enforcement institutions can turn a process meant to provide due process into a trap for people already made vulnerable by the system. There must be accountability and real safeguards to stop immigration enforcement from punishing people for seeking legal protection.
inputs.modified_text: A country has the right to enforce its immigration laws, and filing for legal status should not automatically shield someone from lawful enforcement. But the government must follow its own rules: if court documents show prosecutors acknowledged the May memo did not authorize these arrests, then invoking it anyway is a serious failure of discipline and accountability. Due process is not a loophole or a favor—it is part of the rule of law. Enforce the law firmly, but don’t let agencies stretch their authority and undermine public trust.
